_format: Keys are CSS ids. A key with * is a pattern: * stands for one id segment with no dash (for example a part id like relay3 or inA). Look up the exact key first, then the most specific pattern. A key ending in @stepN (for example #bench@step1) is used on that step only, ahead of the plain key.
#sound-toggle: Turn the workshop sounds on or off. Sound starts off.
#motion-toggle: Calm motion cuts down on animation. The page remembers your choice.
#reset-progress: Start the ladder over from Step 1. You'll be asked to confirm first.
#reset-confirm: Clear all progress, saved modules and benches. Step 1 stays open; every other step locks again.
#reset-cancel: Close this and keep your progress.
#step-nav-1: Step 1: Battery. Go to this step.
#step-nav-2: Step 2: Wire and bulb. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 1.
#step-nav-3: Step 3: Switch. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 2.
#step-nav-4: Step 4: Electromagnet. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 3.
#step-nav-5: Step 5: Relay. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 4.
#step-nav-6: Step 6: Gates. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 5.
#step-nav-7: Step 7: Binary. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 6.
#step-nav-8: Step 8: Half adder, then full adder. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 7.
#step-nav-9: Step 9: 8-bit adder. Go to this step. It unlocks when you finish Step 8.
#prev-step: Go back to the step before this one.
#next-step: Go on to the next step. It unlocks when you finish this one.
#hints-toggle: Show or hide hints for this step.
#tray-cell: Add a zinc and copper cell to the top of your pile. Drag it onto the pile or just tap it (up to 6 cells).
#pile-cell-*: Click to flip this cell over. A flipped cell pushes against the others, so it takes its volt away instead of adding it.
#pile-remove: Take the top cell off your pile.
#tray-pile: Your pile from Step 1, the power for this bench. Drag it onto the bench or tap to place it.
#tray-lamp: A small bulb. Place it on the bench, then wire its two screws into a loop with your pile.
#tray-pull: Open or close the parts drawer. Pick a part from it and bring it over to the bench.
#tray-knife: A knife switch. Wire it into your loop, then tap it on the bench to close or open it.
#tray-knife-a: Switch A, the first input for your gate. Wire it to a relay coil, then tap it to turn A on or off.
#tray-knife-b: Switch B, the second input for your gate. Wire it to a relay coil, then tap it to turn B on or off.
#tray-magnet: An iron nail wrapped in a coil of wire. Wire it to your pile, then use the turns and wire buttons to make it strong enough.
#tray-relay: A relay: current through its coil (c1, c2) flips a switch arm. The common screw connects to normally closed when the coil is off, and to normally open when it's on.
#tray-NOT: Your NOT module from Step 6. Its output is the opposite of its input.
#tray-AND: Your AND module from Step 6. Its output is on only when A and B are both on.
#tray-OR: Your OR module from Step 6. Its output is on when A, B or both are on.
#tray-XOR: Your XOR module from Step 6. Its output is on when exactly one input is on.
#tray-HALF: Your half adder module from Step 8. It adds A and B, giving a sum and a carry.
#tray-FULL: Your full adder module from Step 8. It adds A, B and a carry-in, giving a sum and a carry-out.
#bench-delete: Remove the selected part or wire from the bench. The Delete key works too.
#bench-clear: Take everything off the bench and start this build again. Fixed inputs and bulbs stay put.
#bench: Your workbench. Bring parts over from the tray, then wire them screw to screw.
#bench@step1: Your pile. Add cells to raise the voltage, about 1 volt each. The meter shows the total; a flipped cell pulls it down.
#bench@step7: Eight bulbs, each worth twice the one to its right. Flip a switch to light its bulb; the lit bulbs add up to your number.
#bench-stage: Tap a screw, then another screw, to run a wire between them. Drag a part to move it; tap a switch to flip it.
#magnet-turns-less: Unwind 10 turns of wire, down to 10.
#magnet-turns-more: Wind on 10 more turns, up to 120. More turns make a stronger magnet.
#magnet-wire-insulated: Switch between bare copper and insulated wire. Bare turns touch each other, so the current takes a shortcut and the coil acts like a single turn.
#gate-tab-not: Build NOT from one normally closed relay.
#gate-tab-and: Build AND from two relays in series.
#gate-tab-or: Build OR from two relays in parallel.
#gate-tab-xor: Build XOR from your NOT, AND and OR modules. Unlocks when all three pass.
#test-not: Try your circuit on both rows of the truth table. If every row passes, NOT becomes a module.
#test-and: Try your circuit on all four rows of the truth table. If every row passes, AND becomes a module.
#test-or: Try your circuit on all four rows of the truth table. If every row passes, OR becomes a module.
#test-xor: Try your circuit on all four rows of the truth table. If every row passes, XOR becomes a module.
#bin-bit-0: The bulb worth 1. Click to turn it on or off.
#bin-bit-1: The bulb worth 2. Click to turn it on or off.
#bin-bit-2: The bulb worth 4. Click to turn it on or off.
#bin-bit-3: The bulb worth 8. Click to turn it on or off.
#bin-bit-4: The bulb worth 16. Click to turn it on or off.
#bin-bit-5: The bulb worth 32. Click to turn it on or off.
#bin-bit-6: The bulb worth 64. Click to turn it on or off.
#bin-bit-7: The bulb worth 128. Click to turn it on or off.
#adder-tab-half: Build a half adder from your gate modules.
#adder-tab-full: Build a full adder from your half adder and an OR. Unlocks when the half adder passes.
#test-half: Try your half adder on all four rows of its truth table. If every row passes, it becomes a module.
#test-full: Try your full adder on all eight rows of its truth table. If every row passes, it becomes a module.
#nine-a-bit-0: Bit 0 of A, worth 1. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-a-bit-1: Bit 1 of A, worth 2. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-a-bit-2: Bit 2 of A, worth 4. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-a-bit-3: Bit 3 of A, worth 8. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-a-bit-4: Bit 4 of A, worth 16. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-a-bit-5: Bit 5 of A, worth 32. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-a-bit-6: Bit 6 of A, worth 64. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-a-bit-7: Bit 7 of A, worth 128. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-0: Bit 0 of B, worth 1. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-1: Bit 1 of B, worth 2. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-2: Bit 2 of B, worth 4. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-3: Bit 3 of B, worth 8. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-4: Bit 4 of B, worth 16. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-5: Bit 5 of B, worth 32. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-6: Bit 6 of B, worth 64. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-b-bit-7: Bit 7 of B, worth 128. Click to flip it between 0 and 1.
#nine-slot-0: The slot for bit 0, worth 1. Drop a full adder module here.
#nine-slot-1: The slot for bit 1, worth 2. Drop a full adder module here.
#nine-slot-2: The slot for bit 2, worth 4. Drop a full adder module here.
#nine-slot-3: The slot for bit 3, worth 8. Drop a full adder module here.
#nine-slot-4: The slot for bit 4, worth 16. Drop a full adder module here.
#nine-slot-5: The slot for bit 5, worth 32. Drop a full adder module here.
#nine-slot-6: The slot for bit 6, worth 64. Drop a full adder module here.
#nine-slot-7: The slot for bit 7, worth 128. Drop a full adder module here.
#test-ripple: Check that all eight full adders are in place and the carry chain works, by trying several sums.
#part-*: A part on your bench. Drag it to move it, or tap it to select it. Tap a switch to flip it.
#part-inA: Input A. Tap it to turn it on or off.
#part-inB: Input B. Tap it to turn it on or off.
#part-inC: Carry-in. Tap it to turn it on or off.
#part-out: The output bulb. It lights when your circuit's answer is 1.
#part-outS: The sum bulb. It lights when the sum bit is 1.
#part-outC: The carry bulb (carry-out on the full adder). It lights when the carry is 1.
#term-*-*: A brass screw terminal. Tap it, then tap another screw, to run a wire between them.
#term-*-pos: The plus (+) end of your pile. Tap it, then another screw, to run a wire.
#term-*-neg: The minus (-) end of your pile. Tap it, then another screw, to run a wire.
#wire-*: A wire. It glows when current or a 1 flows through it. Tap it to select it, then Remove selected to take it off.
